correctness.rationale: The exact 15-term zonotope brightness identity follows from planar determinant area. The global maximum is an exact 32768-sign norm comparison, yielding 120 sign-consistent distinct directions; the global minimum reduces rigorously to 105 great-circle pair intersections and yields exactly 12 directed rays. Each arithmetic comparison uses exact Z[phi], including the 250+110sqrt5 and 306+134sqrt5 endpoints. The spherical absolute-product identity and exact 30/30/30/15 angular classes yield the stated first and second moments. The supplied executable was run and verified against direct 2D projected hull areas; no stochastic check is substituted for completeness.

value.rationale: The regular rhombic triacontahedron is a canonical Catalan zonohedron and icosahedral model. Its natural stereological brightness has exact global bounds and a complete, unexpectedly large 120-direction maximum locus against 12 highly symmetric least-bright directions. The second orientation moment supplies a nontrivial dispersion invariant not determined by its known surface area; this is a motivated full classification of sharp equality directions, not an arbitrary sample or routine renaming.
